title: Even one letter (Avot 6:3)
hook: whoever learns even one letter from someone owes them honor
tomorrow: is the way of Torah really just bread, salt and water?

segments.voice: Yesterday, lishmah: for its own sake, and the rest comes unchased. Today closes the week, with a debt you may not know you owe.

Somebody once showed you how to crack an egg with one hand, or a shortcut on a keyboard, or how to breathe before a hard sentence. Thirty seconds of teaching, and you still use it. So what do you owe someone who taught you one tiny thing? Avot has an answer, and it's bigger than thanks.
screen: `ONE HAND, ONE EGG.` → `THIRTY SECONDS OF TEACHING.` → `WHAT DO YOU OWE?`

segments.voice: Avot 6:3: whoever learns from someone a single chapter, a single law, a single verse, a single word, or even one letter, must treat them with honor. The proof is King David. He learned only two things from Ahitophel, and still called him my teacher, my guide, my close friend, words from a psalm. Here's the surprise: in the book of Samuel, Ahitophel later turns against David. The mishnah still holds up what he taught. Now the round, because the week ends here. Four students, and the sieve that chooses: keep the fine flour. David and Jonathan, parted and never ended: love without conditions. A leopard with a face that can blush: bold as a leopard. A reader growing gray over the same page: turn it, turn it. A hundred and one reviews: according to the effort. And Rabbi Meir's word: for its own sake. Look at who taught each one. A sage with a name like a drumbeat. A sage remembered for one line. Avot is full of people remembered for a single sentence. By today's rule, every one of them is owed honor.
screen: `EVEN ONE LETTER.` · `DAVID AND AHITOPHEL.` · `THE WEEK'S ROUND.` · `OWED HONOR FOR ONE LINE.` · then, large: `EVEN ONE LETTER.`

segments.voice: Count on your fingers the people who taught you one small thing: a word, a knot, a recipe, a way of saying sorry. Name each one, and what they taught, a finger at a time. If one name stops you, stay there for the rest of the sit.
screen: `ONE FINGER, ONE TEACHER.` · `NAME WHAT THEY TAUGHT.` · `STAY WITH ONE.`

segments.voice: Even one letter: Avot's measure for a teacher. Learn that much from someone, and you owe them honor.
The week's last line: even one letter is enough to make someone your teacher. Another week of Avot, walked.

howItsDone: Honoring teachers is part of Jewish law and custom: many people quote a teaching in the name of the one who taught it, and Avot 6:3 is studied with the last chapter of Avot on summer Shabbat afternoons.

fork.setup: a former mentor taught you two things that changed your work, then later did you wrong. how did David speak of Ahitophel?
options: he still called him teacher, guide and close friend for what he taught.
he cut the teaching out of his life along with the man.
he kept the lessons but said he'd learned them on his own.
fork.reveal: the mishnah says David called Ahitophel his teacher, his guide, his close friend. honoring what was taught doesn't erase what came after.

what a scholar hears: the mishnah reads Psalm 55's 'my guide and my close friend' as David about Ahitophel, who later turned against him.
